rag.name: Finset.exists_mem_ne
rag.content:
lemma exists_mem_ne (hs : 1 < #s) (a : α) : ∃ b ∈ s, b ≠ a := by
  have : Nonempty α := ⟨a⟩
  by_contra!
  exact hs.not_le (card_le_one_iff_subset_singleton.2 ⟨a, subset_singleton_iff'.2 this⟩)

@[simp] lemma toRight_cons_inr (hb) :

rag.name: Finset.toLeft_cons_inl

rag.name: Finset.strongInduction_eq
rag.content:
@[nolint unusedHavesSuffices] -- Porting note: false positive
theorem strongInduction_eq {p : Finset α → Sort*} (H : ∀ s, (∀ t ⊂ s, p t) → p s)
    (s : Finset α) : strongInduction H s = H s fun t _ => strongInduction H t := by
  rw [strongInduction]

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

informal_statement: For any element $a$ of type $\alpha$, the formula representation of the natural atom of $a$ is equivalent to the negation of the atomic formula of $a$.
informal_proof: The equality holds by reflexivity, as the formula representation of the natural atom of $a$ is definitionally equivalent to the negation of the atomic formula of $a$. This is established directly by the definition of `toFormula` and `Formula.atom`.
